lots.what_it_is: Unsigned brass drum-type compound pocket (field) microscope, probably Continental late 19th century, with built-in mirror and screw focus, in a fitted mahogany case with cotton-packed accessory compartment; plus a separate wooden box with mother of pearl dot and line inlay and purple silk lined lid.
lots.guide_summary: One same-type SOLD at Gowans ($20 hammer, May 2026). UNSOLD ceiling: Dreweatts early 19th century cased field microscope, est GBP 300-500, 0 bids, 2018 (about A$600 at an assumed 2.00). ASKING: Albion J.E. Winspear boxed brass microscope est A$10-40 (result hidden). Snippet-only leads (eBay US$460, McKenzies est A$250-400) are not counted in the range.
lots.working: keep: lowest same-item SOLD = Gowans lot 406648 $20 hammer (May 2026, drum-type brass pocket microscope in a fitted case, which I viewed). $20 / 1.198 = $16.69, round down to $15. flip: likely resale from SOLD evidence is only about $20; less 13% fees ($2.60) and $15 outbound postage leaves about $2.40, / 2.396 = $1, so 0.
lots.confidence_reason: Type is clear and matches one good local SOLD whose photos I viewed, but there is no maker mark, only one same-item sale, and no opened sold result elsewhere.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 close-up: brass drum body with cut-out window, round brass-backed mirror on a pivot with milled knob, coiled spring/screw focus, sliding draw tube; no maker name or number visible on the drum, tube or base in any of the three photos. Fitted wooden case with brass hinges and hooks, small compartment with cotton wool (possibly holding objectives or slides, contents unseen). The second box has inlaid pearl dots and stringing, water ring stain on lid, some lining stains.
lots.condition: Brass lightly tarnished, appears complete as a body; accessories unknown; inlaid box worn with ring stain and lining stains.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there any maker's name or number on the microscope (base, drum or eyepiece)? What is in the cotton-packed compartment (extra objectives, slides)? Does the focus move freely and is the mirror intact?
